κἀρχαιοπρεπή [and ancient-looking] κἀχερουσίους [and of the Acherusian]. With the Persian proper name Αργήστης [Argestes] κἀργήστης [and Argestes] Pers. 208. Most frequent is κἄν contracted from καί and the potential particle ἄν, from which is different κἄν said for καὶ ἐάν, of which there are two examples in Aeschylus, one Eum. 741, the other in the spurious verse Ch. 997. But it must be noted that καί with the particle and its compounds in Aeschylus no more than in other authors admits crasis, which is an indication that the syllable α, which poets use sometimes long sometimes short, was considered long by nature.
